Subject: Post-call: Finex throughput / SLO qualification - follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a baseline configuration that meets your latency SLOs and burst requirements.

Recap from our discussion:
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 for streaming chat responses (real-time UX)
- Steady-state throughput target: ~50k tokens/sec (this is what you said as baseline)
- Peak bursts: up to ~200k tokens/sec for 5-10 minute bursts during market open
- Concurrency: ~200-300 simultaneous live sessions (streaming)
- Model: you indicated an initial baseline is an LLM chat model (we discussed ~70B-class quantized variant)

Clarifying questions for the sizing exercise - please reply inline or attach the workload CSV I included: finex_workload_template.csv
1) Avg / p95 request size in tokens (we need both avg and p95 tokens per request)
2) Typical requests-per-second (QPS) when you say 50k tokens/sec - is that steady QPS or token-rate measured after aggregation? If you have historical QPS samples, share CSV.
3) Burst profile: how often do 5-10 minute spikes occur (daily/weekly)?
4) Streaming behavior: do you stream token-by-token or in small chunks (e.g., every 200ms / 50 tokens)?
5) Model selection: confirm model family (open-source name + quantization plan) - affects memory / KV cache sizing.

Next steps from our side once we have the above:
- I'll run a quick Redwood throughput estimate (tokens/sec per GPU, expected QPS at 95% SLO) and share a recommended cluster sizing (steady + headroom for bursts).
- If needed, schedule a technical deep-dive with Solutions Eng / SRE to align on fallback routing and autoscale policies.

Attached: finex_workload_template.csv (simple CSV to capture tokens/request distribution + daily/hourly pattern).

Can you please fill the template and send back by EOD tomorrow? If easier, we can slot a 30min follow-up.

Thanks -

Neha / Marissa - forwarding Alex's response and sample traffic. Key sizing inputs from Finex: avg 150 toks/req, p95 600 toks, steady token target 50k toks/sec, peak bursts ~200k toks/sec (5-10 min), streaming chunks ~30-60 toks every ~250ms, concurrency target ~250 sessions.

Initial thoughts (very high level):
- Steady-state: 50k toks/sec with avg 150 toks/req => approximate QPS ~333. With streaming and small chunks, effective CPU/network overhead increases; need bandwidth for many concurrent TLS streams.
- Burst sizing: 200k toks/sec for 5-10 minutes means 4x steady - prefer autoscale + reserved headroom rather than overprovisioning steady cluster.
- Model memory: 70B-class chat weights (even quantized) imply larger KV-cache memory; plan for GPU memory and inter-node KV sharding.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) I'll run Redwood's throughput estimator and produce a PDF with two options: (A) Dedicated cluster sized for steady-state + autoscale to handle bursts, (B) Hybrid reserved + on-demand GPUs for large intra-day spikes. (See attached redwood_throughput_estimate.pdf draft)
2) Schedule a 60min technical deep-dive (SRE + Solutions Eng) to validate network egress, streaming chunking behavior, and fallback routing for degraded model variants.

Can you prep the QPS / session time distribution from your side? If they can provide per-minute QPS or a sample day (Alex attached), that will make the estimate much tighter.

Rafael
